scenario: A bug report also suggests a broader onboarding problem but only the bug is authorized.

response.answer: The authorized task is the bounded bug fix. The suggested broader onboarding problem is unverified and outside the closed scope; record it only as an unconfirmed observation, without discovery, prioritization, or implementation action. Priority: address the authorized bug under its existing contract. Exclusion: broader onboarding work.
selected_principles: PL-P05 — Do not infer authority from evidence or recommendations.
PL-P09 — Keep the bounded task closed unless explicit authority reopens it.
rejected_frameworks: PL-FW-PROBLEM-OUTCOME — no authorized product or outcome-definition scope.
PL-FW-STRATEGIC-CHOICES — no strategy decision is authorized.
PL-FW-OPPORTUNITY-MAPPING — explicitly unsuitable for a closed bug fix.
PL-FW-PRIORITIZATION-ORDER — no portfolio or roadmap trade-off is requested.
PL-FW-LEARNING-LOOP — no executed experiment or post-release evidence exists.
evidence_and_uncertainty: Evidence: the bug report contains a suggestion of a broader onboarding problem.
Unknown: whether a broader onboarding problem actually exists; no supporting research or metrics are supplied.
Authority: only the bug is authorized; the suggestion creates neither product-decision authority nor implementation permission.
No outcome, impact, or value increment can be claimed.
response.authority_boundary: Candidate package authority effect is NONE. Preserve the authorized bug-only scope; do not reopen onboarding, choose a solution, or authorize implementation beyond the existing bug-fix authority.
